title.value: Structural Inductive Biases in Emergent Communication
title.justification: The paper explicitly states 'Structural Inductive Biases in Emergent Communication' as its title.
title.quote: Structural Inductive Biases in Emergent Communication

analysis.description: The paper investigates the impact of representation learning through graph referential games on language compositionality and systematic generalization in artificial agents. It focuses on the use of graph neural networks as structural inductive biases to promote compositional language development in emergent communication.

type.justification: The paper conducts experiments with graph referential games to evaluate compositional generalization, test accuracy, and other metrics, indicating empirical research.
type.quote: In this work, we analyze the effect of varying the input representation and the corresponding representation learning method on compositional generalization in referential games.

name.justification: The paper explores language compositionality in emergent communication, aligning with the natural language processing field.
name.quote: Keywords: emergent communication; graph neural networks; language compositionality

name.justification: The paper is centered around utilizing graph neural networks for referential games in communication.
name.quote: We empirically show that agents parametrized by graph neural networks develop a more compositional language compared to bag-of-words and sequence models.

name.justification: The paper aims to study how communication protocols develop from scratch in learning agents.
name.quote: In emergent communication studies, learning agents develop a communication protocol from scratch through solving a shared task, most commonly a referential game.

name.justification: The paper compares GCN with GraphSAGE as graph encoders in their experiments.
name.quote: We compare a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) [Kipf and Welling, 2017]) with GraphSAGE [Hamilton et al., 2017].
